text: {"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"CA","level":"state","category":"rent_increase_limits","status":"in_force","title":"California statewide rent cap (Tenant Protection Act rent limits, as amended by SB 567)","requirement":"An owner of residential real property may not, over any 12-month period, raise the gross rental rate by more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower. The cap is measured against the lowest gross rental rate charged for the unit at any time in the 12 months before the increase takes effect, excluding accepted discounts, incentives, concessions or credits. Where the same tenant stays in occupancy, no more than two increments are allowed in a 12-month period. The owner may set the initial rent for a new tenancy in which no prior tenant remains in lawful possession. Subleases may not produce total rent above the allowable rate. Rent increases require notice under Civ. Code § 827. The gross rent and any discounts must be listed separately in the lease. Waivers are void.
